what_this_is: A matched control pair for an occlusion defect: one frame as the product shipped the audit view, one as PR #1014 fixed it. One camera, one set of geometry bytes, differing only in whether the retained surface is drawn.
why_it_is_not_in_controls_v3: That set covers registration alignment, support crop, and camera framing. Its passing value for the framing dimension is 'reviewable', which conflates being inside the frame with being visible. camera_framing_probe passed this view -- no vertex was cut off -- while 35.2% of its subject was readable, so occlusion needs a dimension of its own.

camera.note: The product's own _view_cameras fitted this for REMOVED_VIEW against the same geometry keys the blueprint supplies. Shared by both frames; the renderer solves one eye distance over the union of both.

measurement.instrument: Pixels the z-buffer awarded to the subject, counted in two passes through the same rasterizer that wrote the delivered PNGs.
measurement.independent_of: audit_view_occlusion.py, which casts rays against a RaycastingScene and reports surface area. Two unrelated instruments on one claim.
measurement.denominator: The subject's screen footprint -- the pixels the rasterizer awards it when nothing else is drawn. audit_view_occlusion.py uses total surface area including back faces, so the two numbers answer different questions and are not expected to match. Both show the defect.

layers_not_committed: The three layer PLYs are 55 MB and are not in Git. Their sha256 above identifies them exactly, and the harness regenerates them from Open3D's published Eagle scan at the recorded seed. Committing 55 MB to make a 660 KB pair reviewable is the wrong trade; the frames, the labels, the measurements, and the provider bundle are all here.
